newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria stock market stagnant for third month.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria stock market stagnant for third month.

text.p: Inaccuracies in registration applications of companies have blocked trade in corporate stocks on the Bulgarian stock market since end-October, a Securities and Stock Exchanges Commission (SSEC) official said.

"Inaccurate information submitted to the commision by candidates for investment intermediaries and by companies that have issued shares has prevented us from licensing them for trading," a SSEC ofiicial told reporters.

Trade was suspended on the Bulgarian Stock Exchange (BSE) on October 23 by the commission because there were no licensed investment intermediaries at the time and no corporate stocks were authorised for floor trading.
Under amendments to the Securities and Stock Exchange Law approved by parliament in June companies that want to trade in shares should register as investment intermediaries with the SSEC.
Only three investment intermediaries have been licensed so far, the SSEC official said. They are Ever, Eurofinance and Ulpia Investment Management financial houses. @
A total of 59 licensing applications have been submitted to the SSEC by the end of 1996.
So far the commission has approved shares of United Bulgarian Bank and the joint Bulgarian-Russian Investment Bank for floor trading.
TBS Hotels stocks were expected to be approved soon, the SSEC official said.

The BSE has not yet received a trading licence bacause it had not raised the minimum capital of 100 million levs required under the Securities and Stock Exchange Law, he added. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
